Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National GreenFaith joins Make Polluters Pay coalition to honour Guterres for climate leadership Source : Kenneth Awotwe Darko 17 November 2026 2:46pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
GreenFaith has joined the Make Polluters Pay International Coalition to honour United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres for his leadership in the global climate movement and his calls for the fossil fuel industry to be held accountable for the climate crisis.
The recognition was presented during the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, in what is expected to be Mr Guterres' final participation in the UN climate negotiations as Secretary-General.
The award acknowledges his sustained advocacy for governments to accelerate the transition away from fossil fuels and ensure that companies responsible for climate damage contribute to addressing its impact.
Representatives of the coalition, including GreenFaith Global Program Director Meryne Warah, Fill the Fund Global Convenor Harjeet Singh, and coalition convenors Louise Hutchins and David Hillman, presented the honour.
At COP31, Mr Guterres renewed his criticism of the fossil fuel industry, declaring that “fossil fuels must go the way of the dinosaurs” and warning that industry lobbying was undermining efforts to address the climate crisis.
He also called on governments to tax windfall profits made by fossil fuel companies and channel the proceeds towards helping vulnerable countries recover from climate-related damage.
“Those who profit most from fossil fuels must help foot the bill for the damage they have caused,” he said.
Mr Guterres cited figures showing that the world's nine largest oil companies made $95 billion in profits in the last quarter alone, while the Loss and Damage Fund had received approximately $600 million.
He argued that taxing these profits would provide resources to support countries facing the devastating effects of climate change.
Speaking on the recognition, Ms Warah said climate justice required protecting lives, dignity and the future of communities affected by the climate crisis.
She noted that people of faith and frontline communities across the world were demanding an end to the destruction caused by fossil fuels and accountability from those who had profited from the industry.
“Guterres has used his platform to speak truth to power, challenge the influence of the fossil fuel industry and remind governments that climate action must be rooted in justice. We are delighted to recognise his contribution to this global struggle,” she said.
Convenor of the Make Polluters Pay International Coalition, Louise Hutchins, said the UN Secretary-General had used his position to confront one of the world's most powerful industries and strengthen calls for accountability.
She said his advocacy had helped advance the global campaign for climate justice and efforts to ensure that communities bearing the greatest costs of the climate crisis receive support.
Other organisations represented in the recognition included Fill the Fund, Stamp Out Poverty, 350.org, Greenpeace International and the Make Big Polluters Pay Alliance Australia.
The groups called on governments to move beyond statements of commitment and introduce legally binding measures requiring major polluters to contribute to addressing climate-related damage.
The recognition comes as climate justice organisations intensify calls for a fairer financing system that places greater responsibility on fossil fuel companies for the environmental damage associated with their operations.
